For k=3, Alt^2(Q) is one-dimensional, giving the projective rank-one family plus one rank-two orbit. For k=2, the induced GL(3) action on Alt^2(Q) is onto GL(3) over an algebraically closed field, so the problem reduces to strict equivalence of faithful 2-by-3 matrix pencils. The listed Kronecker block types match the faithful possibilities; the stored representatives independently satisfy skewness, two-step vanishing, and the stated centre/derived dimensions. Completeness rests on the classical Kronecker canonical-form theorem, not on the package's random spot check.
